page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.xlarge is a compute-oriented cloud instance configured with 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor operating at 3.2 GHz. Hyper-threading provides 2 threads per core using dedicated CPU allocation on a KVM hypervisor. The instance includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support includes AVX, AES, FMA, BMI2, and ADX extensions. The instance contains no bundled local SSD storage and relies on network storage solutions, supported by a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. No discrete GPUs are present.

In performance evaluations, the ecs.c4.xlarge exhibits varied results dependent on thread scaling. Single-threaded tasks reach average throughput, as evidenced by gzip compression speeds of 25.81 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression speeds of 9.42 GB/sec. Multi-core operations rank in lower percentiles across synthetic suites, with stress-ng multi-core recording 2865.78 and Geekbench multi-core scoring 2416.0. Memory bandwidth tests yield 22.04 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 14.84 GB/sec for writes. Small language model text generation on a 135M model operates at 78.7 tokens per second.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU resources, this server provides predictable single-core performance without burstable throttling. The lack of local NVMe storage and moderate memory bandwidth limit its effectiveness for high-throughput databases or memory-intensive analytics. Consequently, the instance functions best for single-threaded processing pipelines, lightweight web server deployments, basic background workers, and entry-level execution utilities.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.xlarge is a compute-focused instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor running at 3.2 GHz across 2 physical cores and 4 dedicated vCPUs. Running on a KVM hypervisor, it provides 8.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per vCPU), a 25 MB L3 cache, and 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with zero local storage. Supported instruction sets include AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA. Benchmark results demonstrate average single-threaded compression performance, such as 25.81 GB/sec in gzip, alongside modest multi-core scoring in Geekbench (2416.0) and stress-ng (2865.78). Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 22.04 GB/sec. The instance delivers steady execution for basic single-threaded batch tasks, light web serving, and legacy enterprise utilities where high memory capacity or local storage speeds are not strictly required.
